units.rhetorical_move: breaks one factor into two sub-metrics
units.function: split a priority before measuring it

original_instantiations: income splits into efficiency and equality
each half then gets its own metric

units.source_excerpt: Breaking income into efficiency and equality, we chose a metric for each.
units.reusable_pattern: Split a priority factor into two parts before naming its metrics.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not measure the factor whole.

units.rhetorical_move: derives a share by dimensional analysis
units.function: name the method that fixed the share

original_instantiations: one occupation's share comes from dimensional analysis
the analysis links productivity to consumption

units.source_excerpt: Through dimensional analysis we found one occupation would take about a quarter of the colony.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute a share to the method that produced it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the share as a guess.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the inequality minuscule

original_instantiations: the inequality coefficient is called minuscule
its value is given in the same sentence

units.source_excerpt: We could achieve an economy with a minuscule amount of income inequality.
units.reusable_pattern: Call a very small coefficient minuscule and give its value.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not upgrade minuscule to zero.

units.rhetorical_move: ranks the output among earthly nations
units.function: place a figure in a percentile

original_instantiations: output per head sits among the top quarter of nations
the figure is also said to match the education model

units.source_excerpt: Our output per head ranks among the top quarter of nations and matches the education model.
units.reusable_pattern: Locate a figure among real nations and cross-check it against another model.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the cross-check.

units.rhetorical_move: prefers a little inequality to a lot of segregation
units.function: state a tradeoff and pick a side

original_instantiations: a little income inequality is preferred
it costs less than the social inequality it prevents

units.source_excerpt: A small amount of income inequality is preferable to a more impactful social inequality.
units.reusable_pattern: State a tradeoff and say which side is preferable.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the tradeoff unresolved.

units.rhetorical_move: tells the client to strongly consider

original_instantiations: the client is told to strongly consider the suggestions
the suggestions are called quantitatively supported

units.source_excerpt: The agency should strongly consider our quantitatively supported suggestions.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a summary by urging the client to strongly consider.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften strongly.

units.rhetorical_move: lists the task as numbered sub-items
units.function: turn the brief into an outline

original_instantiations: the task is broken into numbered items
each item carries a lettered sub-item

units.source_excerpt: For the first task, we were asked to do the following, set out as numbered items.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate a task as a numbered outline.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten the outline into prose.

units.rhetorical_move: borrows a title for the paper
units.function: name the paper after a known work

original_instantiations: the title borrows a well-known phrase
a subtitle then states the method

units.source_excerpt: The title borrows a well-known phrase and adds a methodological subtitle.
units.reusable_pattern: Borrow a title, then add a subtitle that says what was built.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the borrowed title as original.

units.rhetorical_move: argues from a historical image
units.function: justify a ratio with an analogy

original_instantiations: an excess of one sex recalls frontier shantytowns
the analogy argues for an even split

units.source_excerpt: An excess of males harkens back to the shantytowns of the frontier.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a demographic choice with a historical analogy.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the analogy.

units.rhetorical_move: drops the apostrophe

original_instantiations: what's prints without its apostrophe
the sentence otherwise stresses families

units.source_excerpt: The sentence prints whats without an apostrophe.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a dropped apostrophe as part of the voice.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not restore the apostrophe when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: calls food security of the greatest import

original_instantiations: food security is of the greatest import
the phrase justifies a large farming share

units.source_excerpt: Food and nutritional security is of the greatest import.
units.reusable_pattern: Stress one need with of the greatest import.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not modernize import to importance.

units.rhetorical_move: scales a rate after testing values

original_instantiations: several birthing parameters were tested
one stated value was then selected

units.source_excerpt: After testing multiple values, we selected one birthing parameter.
units.reusable_pattern: Report a parameter as chosen after testing multiple values.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide that other values were tried.

units.rhetorical_move: notices the colony would decline
units.function: flag a failure before the fix

original_instantiations: the initial birth rate cannot cover mortality
the colony would therefore decline

units.source_excerpt: We noticed the initial birthing rate was too low, leading the colony into decline.
units.reusable_pattern: Flag a failing run with we noticed before describing the fix.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the failing run.

units.rhetorical_move: breaks off mid-list

original_instantiations: a list of equality types stops mid-phrase
a new sentence begins where the list broke

units.source_excerpt: The list of equality categories breaks off in the middle of a phrase.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a sentence that breaks off mid-list.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not finish the sentence for the writer.

units.rhetorical_move: blames inequality on homophily

original_instantiations: inequality is traced to homophily
homophily is glossed as preferring similar people

units.source_excerpt: Such inequalities arise due to homophily, a preference for similar people.
units.reusable_pattern: Name a mechanism and gloss it in the same sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the term without the gloss.

units.rhetorical_move: drives one coefficient to zero to test

original_instantiations: wages are standardized so the coefficient hits zero
segregation then rises because nothing offsets it

units.source_excerpt: Bringing the inequality coefficient to zero produced greater segregation.
units.reusable_pattern: Test a tradeoff by driving one side to its extreme.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the extreme as the recommendation.

units.rhetorical_move: refuses contrived weights

original_instantiations: artificial weights are rejected
empirical analysis of subgroups supplies them instead

units.source_excerpt: Rather than creating contrived values for weights, we use empirical analysis.
units.reusable_pattern: Reject contrived parameters and name the empirical source.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the weights assumed.

units.rhetorical_move: calls a sameness a strength not a weakness

original_instantiations: using one set of priorities looks like a weakness
it is defended as a strength instead

units.source_excerpt: This aspect is more of a strength than a weakness.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the obvious objection and reverse it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not grant the objection.

units.rhetorical_move: says the curve sits not far off the ideal

original_instantiations: the income curve lies close to the equality line
the gap between them gives the coefficient

units.source_excerpt: Our income curve sits not far off the ideal of complete equality.
units.reusable_pattern: Judge a curve by saying it is not far off the ideal.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace the judgment with a statistic.

units.rhetorical_move: says a trend makes intuitive sense

original_instantiations: one group's preference makes intuitive sense
the reason is that they currently draw salaries

units.source_excerpt: The higher concern for equality makes intuitive sense, since they draw salaries.
units.reusable_pattern: Confirm a result by saying it makes intuitive sense and why.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the intuition.

units.rhetorical_move: shows one inflow reaches a new equilibrium

original_instantiations: one sudden inflow of a stated size is added
the population reaches a new equilibrium and does not collapse

units.source_excerpt: An inflow matching the original settlers reaches a new equilibrium and does not collapse.
units.reusable_pattern: Report a shock by its size and say the population does not collapse.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim this for every shock size.

units.rhetorical_move: lets the reader presume a span
units.function: invite the reader into the calculation

original_instantiations: the reader is asked to presume a stated span has passed
a growth rate is then applied to it

units.source_excerpt: Let us presume that a stated number of years have passed.
units.reusable_pattern: Draw the reader in with let us presume.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the presumption as data.

units.rhetorical_move: gives two timings for the next wave

original_instantiations: the next wave could wait for equilibrium
alternatively it could come sooner, as the population falls

units.source_excerpt: The next wave could wait for equilibrium, or alternatively come sooner.
units.reusable_pattern: Give a timing and then an alternative with alternatively.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the alternative.

units.rhetorical_move: bounds the rescue by spending
units.function: derive a headcount from a budget

original_instantiations: current spending supports a stated number of migrants
the number comes from spending per head

units.source_excerpt: Current spending can support a stated number of migrants, from the spending per head.
units.reusable_pattern: Derive a capacity from a budget divided by spending per head.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not state the headcount without the budget.

units.rhetorical_move: converts growth into longer workdays

original_instantiations: a stated growth forces longer farm workdays
the new workday length is given in hours

units.source_excerpt: If the population grows by a stated share, farmers must work longer days.
units.reusable_pattern: Translate a growth rate into a longer working day.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the cost abstract.

units.rhetorical_move: contrasts strength with weakness in one sentence

original_instantiations: one modelling choice could be read either way
the paper calls it a strength

units.source_excerpt: Using the same priorities for every subgroup is more a strength than a weakness.
units.reusable_pattern: Judge one of your own choices as a strength rather than a weakness.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list it under both headings.

units.rhetorical_move: says a parameter would no longer work

original_instantiations: the assumption of no unemployment stops working
jobs cannot grow as fast as the population

units.source_excerpt: The lack of unemployment would no longer work, since jobs cannot grow like population.
units.reusable_pattern: Say which assumption stops holding and why.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not keep the assumption under the shock.

units.rhetorical_move: compares the burden to any large migration

original_instantiations: the burden matches any large migration
unemployment rises because jobs lag population

units.source_excerpt: As with any large scale migration, unemployment would rise.
units.reusable_pattern: Generalize a result with as with any.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the result is unique.

units.rhetorical_move: doubles a verb

original_instantiations: makes is followed at once by allows
the two verbs say the same thing

units.source_excerpt: The sentence says a model that makes allows us to make recommendations.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep two verbs stacked where one would do.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not delete one of the verbs when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: disagrees with an imagined reader
units.function: reject a view some may hold

original_instantiations: some may envision rapid breeding as best
the group disagrees with that notion

units.source_excerpt: Though some may envision rapid breeding as best, our group disagrees.
units.reusable_pattern: Reject a tempting view by attributing it to some.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not adopt the rejected view.

units.rhetorical_move: says the shares may seem appalling

original_instantiations: the recommended shares may seem appalling
food and health are then called the cornerstones

units.source_excerpt: These values may seem appalling at first glance, yet food and health are the cornerstones.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede that a number may seem appalling, then defend it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the concession.

units.rhetorical_move: separates goods from services

original_instantiations: services go to the government
goods stay in private hands

units.source_excerpt: The government should handle services, with goods-based industries in private hands.
units.reusable_pattern: Split an economy into two sectors and assign each.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the two sectors.

units.rhetorical_move: asserts rather than suggests
units.function: raise the verb for one point

original_instantiations: one recommendation is asserted
the others are only recommended

units.source_excerpt: We assert that a stated leave period moves the colony toward gender equality.
units.reusable_pattern: Raise the verb to assert for the point held most firmly.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten assert to suggest.

units.rhetorical_move: misspells the intake

original_instantiations: intake loses a letter
the sentence otherwise accepts gradual arrivals

units.source_excerpt: The letter accepts a gradual intake and drops a letter from the word.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the misspelled intake.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the spelling when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: closes on a pleasure and an invitation

original_instantiations: helping is called a pleasure
the client is invited to reach out

units.source_excerpt: It has been a pleasure to help, and the client may reach out with questions.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a policy letter with a pleasure and an invitation to reply.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not end on the last recommendation.

units.rhetorical_move: lists sources after the letter
units.function: keep the citations in the paper's own format

original_instantiations: the sources follow the letter
each one carries an access date

units.source_excerpt: The sources are listed after the letter, each with an access date.
units.reusable_pattern: Place the references after the letter.
prohibited_generalizations: The list belongs to this paper and does not transfer.
